speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing pain and swelling in your right knee, as well as painful urination, and you mentioned a previous episode of a swollen ankle. To help me understand what might be causing this, do you have any other joint pain, skin rashes, or eye irritation? Also, have you had any recent urinary tract infections or gastrointestinal illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are sexually active and have had inconsistent condom use, which is very important information. Do you have any eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light, or any skin rashes, particularly on your palms or soles?

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the knee pain and swelling feel worse after resting, such as in the morning or after sitting for a long time? Also, have you noticed any discharge from your penis?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm if you are experiencing any eye symptoms like redness, pain, or light sensitivity, and whether you have noticed any penile discharge. These details are crucial for linking your joint issues with your urinary symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. Given your history of joint swelling and urinary pain, I need to rule out an infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Culture; REQUEST TEST: Gonorrhea and Chlamydia NAAT.

speaker: Doctor
text:
It is unusual for the urinalysis and STI tests to be completely normal given your symptoms, so I need to consider other causes like reactive arthritis triggered by a past infection. Did you have any diarrhea or stomach issues in the weeks before your ankle and knee started hurting?

REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27; REQUEST TEST: ESR and CRP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HLA-B27: Positive; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): 38 mm/h; C-Reactive Protein (CRP): Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive HLA-B27 status and elevated inflammatory markers, combined with your history of asymmetric joint swelling and urinary symptoms, strongly suggest a diagnosis of reactive arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
